findings.quote: Do not touch `supabase/` (no migrations, `9999_init.sql` may be frozen), `apps/web/vercel.json`, `proxy.ts`, or `next.config.ts` (3.4 changes headers).
findings.problem: G5's 2.1a ships the CSP in `apps/web/src/lib/security/csp.ts` with `media-src 'self' blob: https://<supabase host>`. 3.3a's `SermonPlayer`/`LinkPreview` `native_stream` branch (Dropbox `dl.dropboxusercontent.com`, any-https mp3/m4a/mp4/m3u8) renders `<audio src=...>`/`<video src=...>` from arbitrary https hosts, which that CSP blocks on every `(org)` page — yet the prompt forbids the agent from changing the headers. Built as written, linked Dropbox/https sermons cannot play on the admin page and the done_when item 'native audio/video for Dropbox/https streams' is unreachable. G8's own open_issues flags this but leaves it to the assembler instead of fixing the prompt.
findings.fix: In Constraints replace the quoted sentence with: 'Do not touch `supabase/`, `apps/web/vercel.json` or `proxy.ts`. The ONLY header change allowed: in 2.1a's `src/lib/security/csp.ts` widen `media-src` in BOTH variants from `'self' blob: https://<supabase host>` to `'self' blob: https:` (linked recordings stream from arbitrary https hosts — DESIGN §9 lists only the Supabase host), update `src/lib/security/csp.test.ts` accordingly, and record the widening under HANDOFF "Deviations from plan".' Add a matching sentence to Build 9 and a Verify line: `git grep -n "media-src" apps/web/src/lib/security/csp.ts` → shows `https:`. In 3.4 Build 8 change 'media-src 'self' https: (… note the widening vs DESIGN §9)' to 'keep the `media-src 'self' blob: https:` that 3.3a set'.

findings.quote: parse `sermonLinkSchema.extend`-free — parse `sermonDetailsSchema` and `sermonLinkSchema` separately;
findings.problem: Garbled instruction; an agent cannot tell whether it may merge the schemas or not.

findings.quote: `getSignedUrl('sermon-media', storage_path, SIGNED_URL_TTL_SECONDS)` → `{ url, expiresAt }`
findings.problem: 3.1's `getSignedUrl(bucket, path, expiresIn)` (G7) has no documented return shape and may return a bare URL string; the player and 3.4 need `{ url, expiresAt }`, which is exactly what 1.7a's `createSignedUrl(db, bucket, path, { ttl, download? })` returns. Two agents would produce incompatible `media` props.
findings.fix: In Build 7 (`mintSermonMediaUrl`) and Build 9 say: 'mint with `createSignedUrl(createServerSupabase(), 'sermon-media', storage_path, { ttl: SIGNED_URL_TTL_SECONDS })` from `@church/db/queries/storage.ts` (returns `{ url, expiresAt }`); use 3.1's `getSignedUrl` only if it already returns that shape.'

findings.quote: add `maxUploadMb` there via `readMaxUploadMb(process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_MAX_UPLOAD_MB)` if 2.1a did not expose it
findings.problem: G5's 2.1a fixes `publicEnv()` to return `{ supabaseUrl, supabasePublishableKey, appUrl, maxUploadMb }`; the hedge invites a duplicate field.
findings.fix: Replace with: '2.1a's `publicEnv()` already returns `maxUploadMb` (read `src/lib/env.ts`); use it, do not add a second reader.' Apply the same edit to 3.3b Inputs bullet 1.

findings.quote: `mapStorageErrorMessage(message)` → a `DomainErrorKey` such as `file_too_large`, `unsupported_mime_type`, `object_already_exists` (read `packages/domain/src/errors.ts` for the exact keys)
findings.problem: G4's 1.6a fixes `mapStorageErrorMessage(message): StorageErrorKey` with `StorageErrorKey = 'upload_too_large_for_plan' | 'upload_mime_not_allowed' | 'upload_object_exists' | 'upload_failed'` (included in `DOMAIN_ERROR_KEYS`). 3.3b's Build 3/5/11 tests and done_when #2/#5 hard-code `file_too_large`, `unsupported_mime_type`, `object_already_exists`, and also use `network_error` and `cancelled`, which exist in no catalogue. An agent following the tests literally writes keys that `errorMessageFor` does not know.
findings.fix: Everywhere in 3.3b (Build 3, 5, 7, 11, done_when #2 and #5, notes) replace `file_too_large` → `upload_too_large_for_plan`, `unsupported_mime_type` → `upload_mime_not_allowed`, `object_already_exists` → `upload_object_exists`. In Build 5 define `export type UploadErrorKey = StorageErrorKey | 'auth_required' | 'permission_denied' | 'network_error' | 'cancelled'` in `upload-errors.ts` with web-local copy for the last two (not in `@church/domain`), and say `uploadErrorToKey(err): UploadErrorKey`; 413 → `upload_too_large_for_plan` (message computed with the MB number), 415 → `upload_mime_not_allowed`, 409 → `upload_object_exists`, other 4xx/5xx → `upload_failed`.

findings.quote: temporarily set `NEXT_PUBLIC_MAX_UPLOAD_MB=60` locally and try a 55 MB file → the Storage 413 is mapped to the `file_too_large` message (bucket wins)
findings.problem: Build 2 defines the client-side cap as `min(env cap, BUCKETS['sermon-media'].fileSizeLimitBytes)` = 50 MiB regardless of the env value, so a 55 MB file is refused in the browser and never reaches Storage; the 413 path cannot be exercised this way. done_when #2 ('with the env cap raised above the bucket limit, the Storage 413 response is mapped …') is likewise not checkable end to end.
findings.fix: Replace the quoted Verify clause with: 'the Storage 413 mapping is proven by `upload-errors.test.ts` (fake `DetailedError` with status 413 and the Supabase "exceeds the maximum allowed size" body → `upload_too_large_for_plan`); it cannot be reached from the UI because the client cap already includes the bucket limit.' Rewrite done_when #2's second clause to: 'a Storage 413 response (unit-tested with a fake response) maps to the same `upload_too_large_for_plan` message'.

findings.quote: `extensionAndMimeFor(file: File): { ext, mime } | null` — take the lowercase extension from the file name, map it to a canonical MIME (`mp3→audio/mpeg`, …
findings.problem: 1.6a's `limits.ts` already exports `extensionForMime(mime)`, `isAllowedMime(bucket, mime)` and `BUCKETS['sermon-media'].allowedMimeTypes`; a second MIME table in `apps/web` violates 3.3a's 'do not duplicate' rule and can drift from the bucket row. In addition Build 3 says the Server Action validates `ext` 'against the table in item 2', but that function takes a browser `File` and cannot run in a Server Action.
findings.fix: Rewrite Build 2's third bullet as: '`resolveUploadType(fileName: string, reportedType: string): { ext, mime } | null` — pure, string arguments so `planSermonUpload` can call it too: `ext` = lowercase extension of `fileName`; `mime` = `reportedType` when non-empty and `isAllowedMime('sermon-media', reportedType)`, else the canonical MIME for `ext` via a small `MIME_BY_EXTENSION` map (mp3→audio/mpeg, m4a→audio/mp4, aac→audio/aac, wav→audio/wav, ogg→audio/ogg, mp4→video/mp4, m4v→video/mp4, mov→video/quicktime, webm→video/webm) that is checked against `BUCKETS['sermon-media'].allowedMimeTypes` at module load (test asserts every value is allowed); return null when neither is allowed. Reuse `extensionForMime` from `@church/domain` for the reverse direction.' In Build 3 say: 'recompute `{ ext, mime }` with `resolveUploadType(file_name, mime_type)` on the server and reject `null` with `upload_mime_not_allowed`'. Add `resolveUploadType` (not `extensionAndMimeFor`) to Build 7 and Build 11.

findings.quote: `rate_limited` → a page with HTTP 429 semantics ("Too many attempts from this connection — try again in 15 minutes"); `unavailable` → 503 text
findings.problem: A Next.js App Router `page.tsx` cannot set an arbitrary HTTP status; only `notFound()` (404) and `redirect()` are available. An agent will either waste the session hunting for a way to return 429/503 from a Server Component or produce a route handler for the page. done_when #2 ('a 429 text on `rate_limited`') and Goal ('rate-limited probes get a 429 text') read as a status requirement.
findings.fix: Rewrite the clause as: '`rate_limited` → render `src/features/share/RateLimited.tsx` ("Too many attempts from this connection — try again in 15 minutes"; status stays 200 — App Router pages cannot set 429); `unavailable` → render `src/features/share/Unavailable.tsx` ("This link is temporarily unavailable"; status 200). True 429/503 status codes are returned only by the unlock Route Handler (Build 7).' Update Goal and done_when #2 to say 'the rate-limit text' instead of 'a 429 text'.

findings.quote: one text for every reason; for `needs_password_reset` add "The church now requires a password on shared links; ask them for a new link."
findings.problem: `notFound()` carries no payload, so `not-found.tsx` cannot know the reason and cannot add a sentence; the instruction is unexecutable. It also contradicts the Constraints bullet 'All 404-class outcomes share one page and one text (no distinguishing revoked from unknown)'. done_when #2 repeats the extra sentence.

In `ShareLinksPanel` (Build 10) add a status badge 'Needs password (church now requires one)' for links with `requires_password = false` while `sermon_share_requires_password` is on, so leaders learn about it there.

findings.problem: Both G5 2.1a and G7 3.1 fix `requirePerm(ctx, perm | perms[])` where an array means any-of (delegating to `hasAnyPerm`). Build 11 and the notes then use `requireAnyPerm` unconditionally, so two agents end up with two guard APIs for the same check.

Add `canManageShareLinks(ctx) = hasAnyPerm(ctx, ['sermons.link','sermons.upload'])` to `src/features/sermons/perms.ts` with a test.' Replace `requireAnyPerm(ctx, ['sermons.link','sermons.upload'])` in Build 11 with `requirePerm(ctx, ['sermons.link','sermons.upload'])`, drop the `requireAnyPerm` sentence from Inputs bullet 2 ('single key — see Build 1'), and delete the corresponding open_issues entry.

findings.quote: Put the header lists in one module `apps/web/security-headers.ts` (or extend 2.1a's) with a unit test
findings.problem: 2.1a already owns the headers in `apps/web/src/lib/security/csp.ts` + `csp.test.ts`, emitted by two disjoint `headers()` sources (`/((?!s/|embed/).*)` strict and `/(s|embed)/:path*` frameable with `frame-ancestors *`, `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`). 3.4 needs `/s/*` and `/embed/*` to differ (`no-referrer` vs `strict-origin-when-cross-origin`; `noindex, nofollow` vs `noindex`; `Cache-Control: private, no-store` on `/s/*`), which the single frameable source cannot express; a new root-level module would produce duplicate/conflicting header entries.
findings.fix: Rewrite Build 8's last sentence as: 'Do all of this in 2.1a's `src/lib/security/csp.ts`: split the frameable source into two `headers()` entries, `/s/:path*` and `/embed/:path*` (both keep `frame-ancestors *` and no `X-Frame-Options`), giving each the header set listed above; keep the strict source's negative lookahead `/((?!s/|embed/).*)` unchanged. Extend `src/lib/security/csp.test.ts` to assert: `/s/*` → `no-referrer`, `noindex, nofollow`, `private, no-store`, `frame-src https://www.youtube-nocookie.com https://drive.google.com`; `/embed/*` → `strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, `noindex`, no `X-Frame-Options`, no `frame-ancestors 'none'`.' Rename the `security-headers.test.ts` references in Build 12, Verify and done_when #6 to `csp.test.ts`.

findings.quote: a visitor holding a valid cookie is served by re-reading the row with the service client — `sermon_share_links` join `sermons`, `organizations`, `organization_settings` — and re-validating in TypeScript

Two agents would put the join in different places with different column sets.
